clauses.normalized_text: To aid debugging, HTTP caches often append headers to a response detailing how they handled the request.
clauses.raw_text: To aid debugging, HTTP caches often append headers to a response detailing how they handled the request.

clauses.normalized_text: This specification codifies that practice and updates it for HTTP’s current caching model.
clauses.raw_text: This specification codifies that practice and updates it for HTTP’s current caching model.

clauses.normalized_text: To aid debugging, HTTP caches often append headers to a response detailing how they handled the request.
clauses.raw_text: To aid debugging, HTTP caches often append headers to a response detailing how they handled the request.

clauses.normalized_text: Unfortunately, the semantics of these headers are often unclear, and both the semantics and syntax used vary greatly between implementations.
clauses.raw_text: Unfortunately, the semantics of these headers are often unclear, and both the semantics and syntax used vary greatly between implementations.

clauses.normalized_text: This specification defines a single, new HTTP response header field, “Cache-Status” for this purpose.
clauses.raw_text: This specification defines a single, new HTTP response header field, “Cache-Status” for this purpose.

clauses.normalized_text: The key words “MUST”, “MUST NOT”, “REQUIRED”, “SHALL”, “SHALL NOT”, “SHOULD”, “SHOULD NOT”, “RECOMMENDED”, “NOT RECOMMENDED”, “MAY”, and “OPTIONAL” in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [RFC2119] [RFC8174] when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

clauses.normalized_text: This document uses ABNF as defined in [RFC5234], along with the “%s” extension for case sensitivity defined in [RFC7405].
clauses.raw_text: This document uses ABNF as defined in [RFC5234], along with the “%s” extension for case sensitivity defined in [RFC7405].

clauses.normalized_text: The Cache-Status HTTP response header indicates caches’ handling of the request corresponding to the response it occurs within.
clauses.raw_text: The Cache-Status HTTP response header indicates caches’ handling of the request corresponding to the response it occurs within.

clauses.normalized_text: Its value is a List [I-D.ietf-httpbis-header-structure]:
clauses.raw_text: Its value is a List [I-D.ietf-httpbis-header-structure]:

clauses.normalized_text: Cache-Status   = sh-list
clauses.raw_text: Cache-Status   = sh-list

clauses.normalized_text: Each member of the parameterised list represents a cache that has handled the request.
clauses.raw_text: Each member of the parameterised list represents a cache that has handled the request.

clauses.normalized_text: The first member of the list represents the cache closest to the origin server, and the last member of the list represents the cache closest to the user agent (possibly including the user agent’s cache itself, if it chooses to append a value).
clauses.raw_text: The first member of the list represents the cache closest to the origin server, and the last member of the list represents the cache closest to the user agent (possibly including the user agent’s cache itself, if it chooses to append a value).

clauses.normalized_text: Caches determine when it is appropriate to add the Cache-Status header field to a response.
clauses.raw_text: Caches determine when it is appropriate to add the Cache-Status header field to a response.

clauses.normalized_text: Some might decide to add it to all responses, whereas others might only do so when specifically configured to, or when the request contains a header that activates a debugging mode.
clauses.raw_text: Some might decide to add it to all responses, whereas others might only do so when specifically configured to, or when the request contains a header that activates a debugging mode.

clauses.normalized_text: When adding a value to the Cache-Status header field, caches SHOULD preserve the existing contents of the header, to allow debugging of the entire chain of caches handling the request.
clauses.raw_text: When adding a value to the Cache-Status header field, caches SHOULD preserve the existing contents of the header, to allow debugging of the entire chain of caches handling the request.

clauses.normalized_text: The list members identify the cache that inserted the value, and MUST have a type of either sh-string or sh-token.
clauses.raw_text: The list members identify the cache that inserted the value, and MUST have a type of either sh-string or sh-token.

clauses.normalized_text: Depending on the deployment, this might be a product or service name (e.g., ExampleCache or “Example CDN”), a hostname (“cache-3.example.com”), and IP address, or a generated string.
clauses.raw_text: Depending on the deployment, this might be a product or service name (e.g., ExampleCache or “Example CDN”), a hostname (“cache-3.example.com”), and IP address, or a generated string.

clauses.normalized_text: Each member of the list can also have a number of parameters that describe that cache’s handling of the request.
clauses.raw_text: Each member of the list can also have a number of parameters that describe that cache’s handling of the request.

clauses.normalized_text: While all of these parameters are OPTIONAL, caches are encouraged to provide as much information as possible.
clauses.raw_text: While all of these parameters are OPTIONAL, caches are encouraged to provide as much information as possible.

fwd-res       = sh-token
fwd-stored    = sh-boolean
res-fresh     = sh-integer
cache-fresh   = sh-integer
collapse-hit  = sh-boolean
collapse-wait = sh-integer
key           = sh-string

clauses.normalized_text: “fwd” indicates why the request went forward.
clauses.raw_text: “fwd” indicates why the request went forward.

clauses.normalized_text: If it is not present, the value defaults to “none”.
clauses.raw_text: If it is not present, the value defaults to “none”.

clauses.normalized_text: It can have one of the following values:
clauses.raw_text: It can have one of the following values:

clauses.normalized_text: none - The request did not go forward; i.e., it was a hit, and was served from the cache.
clauses.raw_text: none - The request did not go forward; i.e., it was a hit, and was served from the cache.

clauses.normalized_text: bypass - The cache was configured to not handle this request
clauses.raw_text: bypass - The cache was configured to not handle this request

clauses.normalized_text: uri-miss - The cache did not contain any responses that matched the request URI
clauses.raw_text: uri-miss - The cache did not contain any responses that matched the request URI

clauses.normalized_text: vary-miss - The cache contained a response that matched the request URI, but could not select a response based upon this request’s headers.
clauses.raw_text: vary-miss - The cache contained a response that matched the request URI, but could not select a response based upon this request’s headers.

clauses.normalized_text: miss - The cache did not contain any responses that could be used to satisfy this request (to be used when an implementation cannot distinguish between uri-miss and vary-miss)
clauses.raw_text: miss - The cache did not contain any responses that could be used to satisfy this request (to be used when an implementation cannot distinguish between uri-miss and vary-miss)

clauses.normalized_text: res-stale - The cache was able to select a response for the request, but it was stale
clauses.raw_text: res-stale - The cache was able to select a response for the request, but it was stale

clauses.normalized_text: req-stale - The cache was able to select a fresh response for the request, but client request headers (e.g., Cache-Control request directives) did not allow its use
clauses.raw_text: req-stale - The cache was able to select a fresh response for the request, but client request headers (e.g., Cache-Control request directives) did not allow its use

clauses.normalized_text: “fwd-res” indicates what the result of the forward request was.
clauses.raw_text: “fwd-res” indicates what the result of the forward request was.

clauses.normalized_text: It is only valid when fwd is “res-stale” or “req-stale”, and defaults to “full” if not present when fwd is one of those values.
clauses.raw_text: It is only valid when fwd is “res-stale” or “req-stale”, and defaults to “full” if not present when fwd is one of those values.

clauses.normalized_text: It can have one of the following values:
clauses.raw_text: It can have one of the following values:

clauses.normalized_text: full - indicates that the response was a complete response (any status code except 304 Not Modified and 206 Partial Response)
clauses.raw_text: full - indicates that the response was a complete response (any status code except 304 Not Modified and 206 Partial Response)

clauses.normalized_text: partial - indicates that the response was a 206 Partial Response
clauses.raw_text: partial - indicates that the response was a 206 Partial Response

clauses.normalized_text: notmod - indicates that the response was a 304 Not Modified
clauses.raw_text: notmod - indicates that the response was a 304 Not Modified

clauses.normalized_text: “fwd-stored” indicates whether the cache stored the response; a true value indicates that it did.
clauses.raw_text: “fwd-stored” indicates whether the cache stored the response; a true value indicates that it did.

clauses.normalized_text: Only valid when fwd is not “none”.
clauses.raw_text: Only valid when fwd is not “none”.

clauses.normalized_text: “res-fresh” indicates the response’s remaining freshness lifetime (as per [I-D.ietf-httpbis-cache], Section 4.2.1), as an integer number of seconds.
clauses.raw_text: “res-fresh” indicates the response’s remaining freshness lifetime (as per [I-D.ietf-httpbis-cache], Section 4.2.1), as an integer number of seconds.

clauses.normalized_text: This does not include freshness assigned by the cache (see “cache-fresh”).
clauses.raw_text: This does not include freshness assigned by the cache (see “cache-fresh”).

clauses.normalized_text: May be negative, to indicate staleness.
clauses.raw_text: May be negative, to indicate staleness.

clauses.normalized_text: “cache-fresh” indicates the response’s remaining freshness lifetime as calculated by the cache, as an integer number of seconds.
clauses.raw_text: “cache-fresh” indicates the response’s remaining freshness lifetime as calculated by the cache, as an integer number of seconds.

clauses.normalized_text: This includes freshness assigned by the cache; e.g., through heuristics, local configuration, or other factors.
clauses.raw_text: This includes freshness assigned by the cache; e.g., through heuristics, local configuration, or other factors.

clauses.normalized_text: May be negative, to indicate staleness.
clauses.raw_text: May be negative, to indicate staleness.

clauses.normalized_text: If both cache-fresh and res-fresh appear as parameters on the same value, it implies that the cache freshness overrode the response freshness.
clauses.raw_text: If both cache-fresh and res-fresh appear as parameters on the same value, it implies that the cache freshness overrode the response freshness.

clauses.normalized_text: “collapse-hit” indicates whether this request was collapsed together with one or more other forward requests; if true, the response was successfully reused; if not, a new request had to be made.
clauses.raw_text: “collapse-hit” indicates whether this request was collapsed together with one or more other forward requests; if true, the response was successfully reused; if not, a new request had to be made.

clauses.normalized_text: If not present, the request was not collapsed with others.
clauses.raw_text: If not present, the request was not collapsed with others.

clauses.normalized_text: “collapse-wait” indicates the amount of time that the cache held the request while waiting to see if it could be successfully collapsed, as an integer number of milliseconds.
clauses.raw_text: “collapse-wait” indicates the amount of time that the cache held the request while waiting to see if it could be successfully collapsed, as an integer number of milliseconds.

clauses.normalized_text: “key” conveys a representation of the cache key used for the response.
clauses.raw_text: “key” conveys a representation of the cache key used for the response.

clauses.normalized_text: Information about a cache’s content can be used to infer the activity of those using it.
clauses.raw_text: Information about a cache’s content can be used to infer the activity of those using it.

clauses.normalized_text: Generally, access to sensitive information in a cache is limited to those who are authorised to access that information (using a variety of techniques), so this does not represent an attack vector in the general sense.
clauses.raw_text: Generally, access to sensitive information in a cache is limited to those who are authorised to access that information (using a variety of techniques), so this does not represent an attack vector in the general sense.

clauses.normalized_text: However, if the Cache-Status header is exposed to parties who are not authorised to obtain the response it occurs within, it could expose information about that data.
clauses.raw_text: However, if the Cache-Status header is exposed to parties who are not authorised to obtain the response it occurs within, it could expose information about that data.

clauses.normalized_text: For example, if an attacker were able to obtain the Cache-Status header from a response containing sensitive information and access were limited to one person (or limited set of people), they could determine whether that information had been accessed before.
clauses.raw_text: For example, if an attacker were able to obtain the Cache-Status header from a response containing sensitive information and access were limited to one person (or limited set of people), they could determine whether that information had been accessed before.

clauses.normalized_text: This is similar to the information exposed by various timing attacks, but is arguably more reliable, since the cache is directly reporting its state.
clauses.raw_text: This is similar to the information exposed by various timing attacks, but is arguably more reliable, since the cache is directly reporting its state.

clauses.normalized_text: Mitigations include use of encryption (e.g., TLS [RFC8446])) to protect the response, and careful controls over access to response headers (as are present in the Web platform).
clauses.raw_text: Mitigations include use of encryption (e.g., TLS [RFC8446])) to protect the response, and careful controls over access to response headers (as are present in the Web platform).

clauses.normalized_text: When in doubt, the Cache-Status header field can be omitted.
